independent.summary: The parenthesised qualifier is claimed to be "a key no `metadata.name` can reach", but `normalizeTitle` also strips a leading article (`^(the|a|an)\s+`), so a workload/Service/PVC named exactly `a`, `an` or `the` appearing in two namespaces still keys onto a plain name: `a (prod)` normalizes to `prod`, which is exactly the key of a legal object named `prod`. The same two failures the item fixes recur — the second object dropped as `duplicate entity "prod" within the same file`, or `a (prod)` proposed as an `exact-normalized-title` update of a workspace entity titled `prod`. Verified by reading `server/src/lib/similarity.js:79-86`; contrived input, but it is the same defect class left unclosed.

Re-importing a manifest that was already imported under the old dotted titles now forks every qualified entity silently: `cache (prod)` keys `cache prod` against the stored `cache.prod`'s `cacheprod`, which is neither an exact match nor above DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD (trigram Jaccard 0.5 < 0.72, as the new test itself asserts for the hyphenated case), so the item is an unflagged `op: 'create'` with no `duplicate_candidate` flag and no drop reason — a second copy of an entity the workspace already holds, in a producer whose header advertises being safe to re-run. The spec entry declines to re-title already-imported entities but does not account for the unflagged duplicate that follows.
